ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a block placed on a rough horizontal surface indicated by diagonal hatching; from the block there is a force arrow directed obliquely upward to the right, labeled F; the angle between the force and the horizontal dashed line to the right is labeled θ. This indicates that the object is subjected to a pulling force directed upward to the right, the horizontal component makes the object move to the right, the vertical upward component will reduce the normal force, and the friction force is to the left along the horizontal surface. Reasoning: It is known that m=2 kg, μ=0.5, F=20 N, θ=37°, sin37°=0.6, g=10 m/s². From sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8 is obtained. During the action of the force, there is no acceleration in the vertical direction, so N=mg−Fsinθ=2×10−20×0.6=20−12=8 N. The kinetic friction force f=μN=0.5×8=4 N. The horizontal component of the pulling force is Fcosθ=20×0.8=16 N, so the horizontal resultant force is 16−4=12 N. By Newton's second law, a=12/2=6 m/s². In the first 4 s, the object starts from rest and undergoes uniformly accelerated motion, with displacement s1=(1/2)at²=(1/2)×6×4²=48 m, and the speed at the end of 4 s is v=at=6×4=24 m/s. After F is removed, the normal force in the vertical direction becomes N=mg=20 N, the friction force f=μmg=0.5×20=10 N, and the magnitude of the deceleration produced is a2=f/m=10/2=5 m/s². The displacement afterward until stopping is s2=v²/(2a2)=24²/(2×5)=576/10=57.6 m. The total distance is s=s1+s2=48+57.6=105.6 m.

method.method_draft: Use a free-body diagram and constant-acceleration kinematics. First read the image as a block on a rough horizontal surface pulled up and to the right by force F at angle θ above the horizontal, so the vertical component of F reduces the normal force and friction acts leftward. From the text read m=2 kg, μ=0.5, F=20 N, θ=37°, sin37°=0.6, g=10 m/s², initial rest, and force duration 4 s. Compute cos37°=0.8. Vertical equilibrium while the force is applied gives N=mg−Fsinθ=20−12=8 N, so kinetic friction is f=μN=4 N. Horizontal Newton’s law gives net force Fcosθ−f=16−4=12 N, hence a=12/2=6 m/s². For the first 4 s, use s1=1/2 at²=48 m and v=at=24 m/s. After the force is removed, the normal becomes mg and friction is μmg=10 N, so deceleration is 10/2=5 m/s². Stopping distance is s2=v²/(2·5)=57.6 m. Total distance s1+s2=105.6 m.

The coefficient of kinetic friction between the object and the surface is $\mu=0.5$. A force $F=20N$ is applied to the object at an angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$ (where $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$) above the horizontal, as shown in the figure ($g=10\mathbf{m}/\mathbf{s}^{2}$). 1. The acceleration of the object's motion. 2. If the force $F$ is removed after the object has moved for 4 seconds, what is the total distance traveled by the object?
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, there is a block placed on a rough horizontal surface indicated by diagonal hatching; from the block there is a force arrow obliquely upward to the right, labeled F; the angle between the force and the horizontal dashed line to the right is labeled θ. This indicates that the object is subjected to a pulling force upward to the right, the horizontal component makes the object move to the right, the vertical upward component will reduce the normal force, and the friction force is to the left along the horizontal surface.

Reasoning: Given m=2 kg, μ=0.5, F=20 N, θ=37°, sin37°=0.6, g=10 m/s². From sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8 is obtained. During the action of the force, there is no acceleration in the vertical direction, so N=mg−Fsinθ=2×10−20×0.6=20−12=8 N. The kinetic friction force f=μN=0.5×8=4 N. The horizontal component of the pulling force is Fcosθ=20×0.8=16 N, so the horizontal resultant force is 16−4=12 N. By Newton's second law, a=12/2=6 m/s².

In the first 4 s, the object starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration, the displacement s1=(1/2)at²=(1/2)×6×4²=48 m, and the velocity at the end of 4 s is v=at=6×4=24 m/s. After F is removed, the vertical normal force becomes N=mg=20 N, the friction force f=μmg=0.5×20=10 N, and the magnitude of the deceleration produced is a2=f/m=10/2=5 m/s². The displacement afterward until stopping is s2=v²/(2a2)=24²/(2×5)=576/10=57.6 m. The total distance is s=s1+s2=48+57.6=105.6 m.
